tasks.short: Estimate freight rates and record costs and weights

steps.what: Capture shipment weights and service details and select the applicable rate version
Estimate freight or postal rates using checked inputs and applicable tariff rules
Check exceptions and record shipment costs and weights in the shipment record

tasks.design: Configure rate calculation in {OPS_SYSTEM} from checked shipment details and maintained tariff tables. The agent retains weighing or evidence capture, rate applicability checks and final recording; ambiguous services and special cargo go to manual rating.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rate-table lookup and arithmetic can be repeated outside the shipment system.
tasks.enabler_now: Native rating rules can calculate from explicit weights, dimensions, lanes and service conditions.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear tariff applicability, special cargo and missing or inconsistent weight evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when the standard tariff does not describe the actual shipment.
tasks.altitude: The agent may spend less time on arithmetic while retaining estimate responsibility and exception handling.

evidence.claim: Deterministic rating from checked shipment fields and versioned tariffs is plausible, but local configuration and time savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is a shipment estimate and its cost/weight record, excluding rate negotiation, customer quotation release and final invoicing.

Customer or shipper supplies existing shipment details and weight evidence before s1. The agent checks or measures and captures shipment ID, origin, destination, service, pieces, gross weight, dimensions, units and relevant cargo conditions in s1; measurement and capture time stay counted.

The pricing owner supplies existing approved tariff tables with version, validity dates, lane/service scope, chargeable-weight rule, rounding, currency, minimum charge, surcharge conditions and tax treatment. S1 selects and checks applicability. Missing or ambiguous rules stop automatic rating; manual estimation remains available.
Test native rating configuration before custom code. Existing automatic rating runtime earns no new saving.
Allow 8 focal hours per 100 baseline for rating exceptions and sampled recalculation, and 4 other-role hours for tariff maintenance; no free transferred tariff-entry work is assumed.
unknowns: Quality and format of tariff data
research_questions: Do checked native calculations reduce rating effort after tariff maintenance and manual exception handling?

already_counted.description: Weight and shipment capture and applicability checks remain counted
Estimate review and final record remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain approved tariff rules and versions

approvals.approved_version: Exact shipment estimate, weight evidence, rating-input snapshot and tariff version; any changed input or rate voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70; gross saving 30 less 8 focal upkeep gives net 22. Range 5-14 assumes manual lookup/arithmetic today and a material share of special-cargo or incomplete-tariff exceptions; already rated shipments gain zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep goods movement and storage records

steps.what: Capture and check records of goods shipped, received and stored
Copy checked goods events into the consolidated shipment and storage register
Reconcile goods records and investigate missing or conflicting movement evidence

tasks.design: Keep one goods-event register in {OPS_SYSTEM} and replace a duplicate {SPREADSHEET} register with a configured view or sync. The agent still captures and checks evidence and resolves missing events; a scan or system record is not treated as proof that missing goods are present.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate shipment and storage registers can repeat the same entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing transport and warehouse systems provide records that can share a configured register.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded handovers, wrong identifiers and discrepancies between records and physical goods.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving what actually happened when evidence conflicts.
tasks.altitude: The agent may avoid a duplicate register while retaining event accuracy and reconciliation responsibility.

reach.task: Provide a verified movement history for a shipment enquiry
reach.learn: Event provenance and limits of recorded status

evidence.claim: Boltrics provides warehouse, transport and forwarding software, supporting examination of native records configuration without proving this exact duplicate-register removal.

assumptions: Boundary is keeping goods records, excluding physical handling, rate recording and the lost-shipment investigation task. A roll-up assigns shared evidence capture once.

Warehouse handlers and carriers produce existing movement/storage evidence during their unchanged work before s1. The agent checks and captures shipment ID, item or handling-unit ID, quantity, unit, event type, event time, actual location, source reference and event identifier/version in s1. All capture time stays counted.

S2 copies only checked events using unique event IDs; no received, shipped or stored flag is inferred from a planned movement. Missing identifiers, duplicate events and corrections return to manual reconciliation in s3.
Test a native consolidated view before custom sync. This scenario requires an actual duplicate register; an already unified system earns no new saving.
Allow 8 focal hours per 100 baseline for mapping upkeep, sync exceptions and register checks, plus 2 other-role hours for access and connector administration.
unknowns: Availability and reliability of event IDs
research_questions: Does a single register reduce effort after record corrections, event deduplication and reconciliation?

already_counted.description: Goods-event capture and evidence checking remain counted
Reconciliation and missing-event investigation remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain mappings and resolve sync and register exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75; gross saving 25 less 8 focal upkeep gives net 17. Range 3-10 assumes a duplicate register remains but missing evidence and corrections still require manual work; a unified existing register gains zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify freight or baggage arrival, recipient details and the exact arrival notice
Notify the consignee, passenger or customer of confirmed freight or baggage arrival
Arrange delivery with the recipient and carrier and resolve notice exceptions

tasks.design: Configure {OPS_SYSTEM} to send the agent-confirmed arrival notice through {EMAIL}. Keep delivery arrangements, address clarification and failed-notice handling with the agent; an arrival message does not promise clearance or release of cargo.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routine arrival messages may be composed and sent individually after checking arrival.
tasks.enabler_now: A fixed notice can be populated and sent from confirmed fields without a language model.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong contacts, delivery restrictions and cargo that has arrived but is not available for release.
tasks.human_edge: Clarifying the recipient's actual delivery needs and resolving exceptions.
tasks.altitude: The agent may send less repetitive mail but retains recipient verification and delivery coordination.

reach.task: Coordinate a feasible delivery window with the recipient
reach.learn: Release restrictions, delivery access and carrier commitments

evidence.claim: Sending a fixed arrival notice from checked fields is a plausible native workflow; local reliability and savings remain unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is arrival notification and delivery arrangement, excluding customs clearance, cargo release approval and physical delivery. Shared arrival-event capture belongs to one task in a roll-up.

The carrier or terminal produces existing actual arrival evidence before s1 and the customer supplies existing contact details. In s1 the agent checks and captures shipment ID, actual arrival time and place, recipient identity/contact, cargo availability wording, exact template/message version and send timing. All capture and approval effort stays counted.

S2 sends only the confirmed message to the exact confirmed contact. Missing arrival evidence or contact details requires manual notification; no structured arrival or release flag is assumed without checking its source.

The recipient and carrier produce delivery requirements and commitments during s3 after notification. The agent captures and verifies any delivery address in s3; no free structured address or automatic booking is assumed.
Test native notifications first. Already automated notices yield zero new saving.
Allow 6 focal hours per 100 baseline for template upkeep, failed delivery checks and access exceptions; no coordination work is transferred for free.
research_questions: Do configured notices reduce effort after contact checking, failed sends and recipient clarification?

already_counted.description: Arrival, contact and exact notice verification remain counted
Delivery arrangement and notice exceptions remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain notice templates and check send failures

approvals.approved_version: Confirmed arrival notice snapshot, shipment ID, wording, recipient/contact and send timing; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80; gross saving 20 less 6 upkeep gives net 14. Range 2-8 assumes routine manual notices today and substantial contact or release-wording exceptions; delivery coordination remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Retrieve stored items and trace lost shipments

steps.what: Retrieve shipment records and last recorded storage or movement evidence
Trace lost shipments by reconciling evidence and contacting responsible handlers or carriers
Retrieve stored items at the verified location and confirm item identity

tasks.design: Use a native trace view in {OPS_SYSTEM} to bring existing movement records and available carrier references together. The agent checks gaps, contacts handlers and retrieves the actual items; last recorded location is displayed as evidence rather than current physical truth.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful movement evidence can be scattered across records and carrier portals.
tasks.enabler_now: A configured trace view may reduce repeated lookups without automating the investigation.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded transfers, wrong labels and physically locating the missing goods.
tasks.human_edge: Following inconsistent evidence and confirming the actual item found.
tasks.altitude: The agent may locate records faster; tracing judgement and physical retrieval remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare an evidence-based shipment trace for carrier escalation

evidence.claim: A native view of existing movement evidence may reduce repeated lookup time, but this exact cross-system trace and its saving are unmeasured.
Portbase provides import-status information; that capability supports one source of shipment evidence, not proof of current physical location or completed retrieval.

assumptions: Boundary combines record lookup, lost-shipment investigation and the agent's own physical retrieval where assigned. Warehouse crew labour is outside this denominator and is not newly transferred.

Existing goods-recording staff and carriers produce movement records before s1 with shipment/handling-unit ID, event type, time, location and source reference. Their capture work is unchanged and assigned once under record keeping. In s1 the agent captures the enquiry identifier and checks identity, provenance and missing events within retained lookup time.
No current-location flag or loss code is inferred from the last scan. Missing records require portal lookup, telephone contact and physical search in s2/s3; those steps keep their full time.
The verified location is produced in s2 before s3. Unresolved lost cases do not proceed to retrieval; shares represent a workload mix, not successful recovery for every case.
Test native trace views before custom integration. If lookup is already consolidated, incremental saving is zero.
Allow 3 focal hours per 100 baseline for view upkeep and access exceptions, plus 1 other-role hour for connector administration.
unknowns: Existing trace view and portal access
research_questions: Does consolidated evidence reduce lookup time without hiding gaps or increasing false-location searches?

already_counted.description: Identifier capture and evidence checking remain in lookup
Trace investigation and physical retrieval remain fully counted

incremental.description: Maintain view and resolve access exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92.5; gross saving 7.5 less 3 focal upkeep gives net 4.5. Range 0-3 assumes fragmented lookups today, with substantial unrecorded movements and physical search unchanged; already consolidated lookup yields zero.

role.altitude: Configured rating, single records and routine notices may reduce repetitive entry; evidence checks, delivery arrangements and physical tracing remain central.
role.ambitious_version: Use one checked shipment record to support reliable costs and communication while keeping uncertainty and physical goods handling visible.
